description: Comparative matrix contrasting Judaism, Christianity, and Islam across 10 foundational theological and historical dimensions.

themes.judaism: Absolute, non-composite, incorporeal unity (Yihud Ha-Shem). Rejects Trinity and Incarnation as blasphemous/impossible.
themes.christianity: Trinitarian monotheism: One God in three co-equal, consubstantial persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit).
themes.islam: Strict Tawhid (Tawhid al-Rububiyyah, al-Uluhiyyah, al-Asma' was-Sifat). Rejects Trinity (Shirk) and Incarnation.

themes.judaism: Tanakh (Written Torah) accompanied by Sinai Oral Torah; open to rabbinic dialectical interpretation and progressive rabbinic enactment.
themes.christianity: Old and New Testaments; inspired scripture fulfilling Old Testament covenants through Christ.
themes.islam: The Qur'an as literal uncreated verbatim speech of Allah revealed to Muhammad via Jibril; earlier scriptures corrupted (Tahrif).

themes.judaism: No Original Sin dogma. Humans are born morally neutral with Yetzer Ha-Tov and Yetzer Ha-Ra; free will is absolute.
themes.christianity: Original Sin inherited from Adam; humanity is fallen and unable to attain salvation without divine grace in Christ.
themes.islam: Fitrah (innate primordial monotheistic human purity); no inherited guilt; Adam erred and was forgiven upon repentance.

themes.judaism: Sin is rectified directly through Teshuvah (remorse, cessation, confession, restitution), prayer, and charity without vicarious human sacrifice.
themes.christianity: Atonement achieved through the vicarious, substitutionary sacrificial death and bodily resurrection of Jesus Christ.
themes.islam: Forgiveness obtained directly from Allah through sincere repentance (Tawbah), good deeds (Hasanaat), and divine Rahmah.

themes.judaism: Awaits mortal human Davidic King Messiah who will rebuild Temple, gather exiles, and bring universal peace.
themes.christianity: Jesus is the divine Messiah and Savior who accomplished spiritual redemption and will return in the Second Coming.
themes.islam: Isa al-Masih is a revered prophet/messenger who was not crucified (Qur'an 4:157), was raised to heaven, and will return before Judgment Day.

themes.judaism: Ceased in 70 CE due to halakhic prohibition of sacrificing outside Temple Mount (Deut 12); replaced by prayer and repentance.
themes.christianity: Sacrifices permanently fulfilled and abolished once for all by the final sacrifice of Christ on the cross (Hebrews 10).
themes.islam: Animal sacrifice continues as non-atoning devotional commemoration during Eid al-Adha (Udhiyah/Qurbani).

themes.judaism: Halakha: 613 Mitzvot binding exclusively upon the Jewish people; Gentiles obligated only in 7 Noahide Laws.
themes.christianity: Freedom from Mosaic ritual law; moral commandments retained through the Law of the Spirit / Love of Christ.
themes.islam: Sharia: Comprehensive divine legal code (Halal/Haram) binding upon all Muslims globally.

themes.judaism: Righteous of all nations have a share in the World to Come (Olam Ha-Ba); no eternal hellfire dogma.
themes.christianity: Eternal life granted to believers through faith in Jesus Christ; eternal separation/hell for the unredeemed.
themes.islam: Paradise (Jannah) for monotheistic believers; Hell (Jahannam) for disbelievers (Kuffar), with varying scholarly views on permanence.

themes.judaism: Har Ha-Bayit (Mount Moriah): holiest site on earth, place of First/Second Temples and Holy of Holies; direction of all prayer.
themes.christianity: Holy city of Christ's passion, death, and resurrection; Church of the Holy Sepulchre.
themes.islam: Al-Haram al-Sharif / Al-Quds: third holiest sanctuary (Masjid al-Aqsa and Dome of the Rock), destination of Isra and Mi'raj.

themes.judaism: Particularist covenant with a specific historical people (Am Yisrael) tied to a specific geographical Land (Eretz Yisrael).
themes.christianity: Universal spiritual body (Ecclesia) transcending ethnic and geographic national boundaries.
themes.islam: Universal global community of believers (Ummah) transcending race and nation.
